lines: Opens an HTTP server on this machine through which an outside program can read and change the patch: list, add, move and delete modules, patch and unpatch cables, set any knob and read voltages
Starts the server on the first press; there is nothing on the panel that stops it again, and a second press does nothing while it is running
Takes the left channel of a signal to be measured; the voltage here is written into a buffer that the server's audio endpoints read, and it goes nowhere else
Takes the right channel of a signal to be measured; the voltage here is written into a buffer that the server's audio endpoints read, and it goes nowhere else
Note — the module does nothing at all until the Start button is pressed, and on its own it only answers HTTP requests: something has to be at the other end of the connection for anything to happen
Note — the maker's own client is an MCP server and a Claude skill, given out through the Patreon page named in the module's browser entry, and they are not part of this plugin
Note — the orb at the top is red while the server is stopped and green while it is running; it is drawn by the module rather than being a lamp, so it cannot be clicked
Note — the server accepts connections only from 127.0.0.1, this machine itself, so nothing on the network can reach the patch through it
Note — the port is 7777 unless the environment variable NTR_WABOT_PORT is set to another number before Rack is started; the panel prints 7777 whatever the port actually is
Note — setting the environment variable NTR_WABOT_TOKEN before Rack is started makes the server refuse any request that does not carry that same string in an X-Wabot-Token header
Note — the two audio jacks are read whether or not anything is patched to them, and they change nothing in the patch: they exist so that the far end of the connection can measure a signal
Note — the audio endpoints give a spectrum on a twelfth-of-an-octave grid from 20Hz up, and a loudness and stereo reading that needs a few seconds of signal before it will answer

0.why: src/NTR_Wabot.cpp process() reads inputs[j].getVoltage() with no channel into audioRing[0], and the loudness meter scales it by 0.1 so that 10V is full scale

1.why: src/NTR_Wabot.cpp process() reads inputs[j].getVoltage() with no channel into audioRing[1], and the loudness meter scales it by 0.1 so that 10V is full scale

Wabot.notes: Read from the maker's source and README at commit 9dbb673, the head of main. Two commits carry the installed 2.10.0: 7f87299 and 9dbb673. The binary settles it as 9dbb673, which added the configurable port and the optional token: the installed plugin.dylib holds the strings NTR_WABOT_PORT, NTR_WABOT_TOKEN, X-Wabot-Token and the message invalid or missing X-Wabot-Token, none of which exist at 7f87299. The panel SVG is empty; every mark on it is drawn in NTRWabotWidget::draw, so the names were taken from the nvgText calls there and checked against the VCV library screenshot at 400 pixels. The panel prints Start beside the button, Port and 7777 above it, L and R over the jacks and Analyze beneath them. The printed 7777 is a literal in draw() and does not follow wabotPort(), so a rack started with NTR_WABOT_PORT set shows a port number the module is not using; this is in a Note rather than on a control line, because the number is not a control and nothing can be clicked on it. The Start button starts the server and nothing else: stopServer() is called only from the destructor, so the server runs until the module is removed or Rack is closed, and startServer() returns at once if it is already running. Three status lights are configured and set every sample, but no LightWidget is ever added, so they cannot be seen or clicked; the orb drawn in draw() shows the same state and is not a widget either. The module has no context menu of its own, so there are no menu lines. There are no outputs.
